title: Enact definition file
description: A definition file declares the use cases and groups of an Enact application. Files are listed under `enact.definitions` and default to `optional:classpath:enact/`. A file declares `use-cases` and `groups` at its root, without the `enact` prefix; anything else is rejected with the line it is on. A use case name and a group name are each declared once across every file.

use-cases.description: Use cases by name. The name is also the name of the `UseCase` bean the use case is registered as.

groups.description: Groups by name. A group holds what its use cases share: the filters wrapping them and their observability.

group.title: Group
group.description: Settings shared by the use cases of a group. The group named `default` applies to every use case without a `group`.

filters.description: Names of the filter beans wrapping the group's use cases, outermost first; the trigger type defines their kind (`HandlerFilterFunction` for the REST trigger).

observability.description: Observability for the group's use cases; unset inherits `enact.observability`.

useCase.title: Use case
useCase.description: A use case: a typed directed graph of steps, registered as an injectable `UseCase<Input, Output>` bean and optionally exposed through a trigger.

group.description: Group the use case belongs to; `default` when not set.

trigger.description: Optional trigger exposing the use case (e.g. as an HTTP endpoint), as a single entry keyed by trigger type, e.g. `rest`. Its value stays a tree until the `TriggerHandler` claiming that type reads it into its own definition. Without a trigger, the use case can only be injected.

observability.description: Observability for this use case; unset inherits its group, then `enact.observability`.

output.description: Step whose output the use case returns; inferred when not set as the only one nothing reads. Steps that run aside are ignored, and feeding a step that runs aside does not use a value up.

concurrent.description: Whether steps that do not read each other run at once. Off by default: a step moved off the caller's thread leaves any surrounding transaction, `SecurityContext` and MDC behind.

steps.description: Steps in declaration order; each may only bind to one declared before it, so declaration order is already a topological order and a cycle cannot be written.

stepReference.title: Step reference
stepReference.description: One node of the use case's graph: the step to execute, where each of its inputs comes from, and when it runs.

step.description: Name of the step bean to execute.

id.description: Identifies the step within the use case; defaults to `step`, so a step used twice needs one.

in.description: Where the step's inputs come from: `$input` for the use case's own input, `$<step id>` for another step's output. Either one reference for a step taking a single parameter, or one per parameter by name. Left out, a single parameter reads the step declared before it.

oneOf.description: One reference, for a step taking a single parameter.
One reference per parameter, keyed by parameter name. Only a step written as an annotated method can take several parameters.

when.description: SpEL deciding whether the step runs, e.g. `"#coupon != null"`. Each of the step's inputs is readable by parameter name, and `#input` names the only one of a step taking a single parameter. A skipped step is not observed.

else.description: What the step yields when `when` does not hold: `$<parameter>` to pass one of its own inputs through, or a value of its output type. Inferred when not set, as the only input that can stand in for the output. Needed only when another step reads this one.

side.description: Whether the step runs aside: always off the caller's thread, never waited for and never read, so its failure is logged and recorded rather than reaching the caller.

settings.description: Optional step settings (retry, cache). Values set here override those declared on the step.

retry.description: Retries the step until it succeeds or the policy gives up.

cache.description: Caches the step's result; a hit skips the step and its retries entirely.

retry.title: Retry
retry.description: Retry policy of a step, built on `org.springframework.core.retry`.

includes.description: Fully qualified exception class names to retry on; every exception when empty.

excludes.description: Fully qualified exception class names never to retry on.

max-retries.description: Maximum number of retries after the first attempt.

timeout.description: Time after which no further retry is started; zero means no timeout.

delay.description: Base delay before the first retry.

jitter.description: Maximum random amount added to each delay.

multiplier.description: Factor the delay is multiplied by after each attempt.

max-delay.description: Upper bound the multiplied delay never exceeds.

cache.title: Cache
cache.description: Caches the step's result in the application's `CacheManager`, which must know the cache name.

name.description: Name of the cache in the application's `CacheManager`.

key.description: SpEL expression evaluated against the step input (`#input`). Defaults to the input itself.

enabled.description: Whether use case and step observations are recorded. Unset inherits: a use case falls back to its group, a group to `enact.observability.enabled`, which defaults to `true`.

restTrigger.title: REST trigger
restTrigger.description: REST HTTP endpoint trigger, bound from `trigger.rest` and handled by `enact-starter-web`. By default, path variables and matching query parameters are bound to input properties of the same name and the JSON body to the input itself; `bind` declares anything else. `rest:` without a body takes every default.

path.description: URL path for the REST endpoint. May contain path variables, e.g. `/orders/{id}`.

bind.description: Input property to request source: `header:<name>`, `query:<name>`, `path:<name>`, `attribute:<name>` (a request attribute, e.g. set by a filter), `body` or `body:<json-pointer>`, e.g. `tenantId: header:X-Tenant-Id`.

filters.description: Names of `HandlerFilterFunction` beans applied after the filters of the use case's group.

status.description: HTTP status code for successful responses.

duration.description: A duration in the format Spring Boot accepts elsewhere in the configuration, e.g. `100ms`, `2s`, `PT1M`, or a plain number of milliseconds.
